problems: Blind guess was a sailing ship, not a gull. The silhouette's vertical body with a pointed top and flared base at the bottom reads as a hull or mast, which is probably why it was misread. Only the alternative guess (bird in flight) is right.
The silhouette is a set of thin double outlines, not a solid shape, so it reads as a wireframe rather than a bird silhouette.
Head star 5434 (~245,223) sits on the top of the body, but the body is so narrow and pointed that there is no distinct head or neck.
Right wing elbow 3414 (~367,224) and tip 2225 (~447,288) sit on the right wing outline, which is reasonable.
Left wrist 7607 (~116,181) sits on the lower edge of the raised left wing and the left wing tip 8068 (~96,122) is correctly at the top-left extremity.
Inner primary 2900 (~404,290) and right wing tip 2225 (~447,288) have overlapping labels: 'inner primary feathers of the right wing' runs into 'tip of the right wing'. The text is unreadable.
Tail root 5317 (~254,313) is at the base of the body, but the forked tail at the bottom (~235-272, 310-346) is small and does not visibly fan out.
output.advice:
Redraw so the figure reads unambiguously as a gull in flight, not a ship. Keep the current star placements, but change the silhouette around them.
1) Head and neck: make a rounded head around 5434 (~245,223) with a short, slightly forward-angled neck. Drop the pointed peak above it so there is no mast-like spike.
2) Body: a tapered, slightly thicker torso running from the head down to 5317 (~254,313). Keep it solid, not a double line.
3) Tail: at 5317, fan the tail out into a wide, shallow fork of about 25-30px spread (roughly x 235-275, y 310-335). Remove the flared hull-like base.
4) Raised left wing: a broad, filled wing running from the shoulder near the body (~240,225) up-left to tip 8068 (~96,122), with the wrist 7607 (~116,181) on the leading edge where it bends. Give the trailing edge a few feather notches.
5) Spread right wing: a broad wing from the shoulder near (~250,230) out through the elbow 3414 (~367,224) to tip 2225 (~447,288), with inner primaries 2900 (~404,290) along the trailing edge. Make the wing about 30-40px deep so it reads as a solid shape.
6) Labels: move the 'inner primary feathers' label below the wing (e.g., around y 320-330, x 380) and the 'tip of the right wing' label above the tip, so they no longer overlap. Keep the title and the other labels as they are.
7) Keep the gold skeleton lines as guides only. The final figure should be a filled or outlined bird silhouette, not a copy of the gold lines."
